note: Pins of pmml, PushMPC's ML runtime layer (pmml/). Everything here is fetched from its official source (nuget.org, pypi.org, GitHub releases of the upstream project) by pmml/scripts/fetch_runtime.py, at install time on the user's machine and on CI, and checked against the SHA-256 below. An entry whose sha256 is TODO is fetched only with --allow-unpinned (CI prints the hash; nothing unpinned ships). Wheels are used as archives: only their native libraries (and licence files) are extracted; Python is never needed to run them. Layout under the runtime folder: ort/<flavor>/ (one ONNX Runtime per flavor, one flavor per process), eps/<ep>/ (plugin execution providers with an ep.json), ncnn/, models/.

core.what: ONNX Runtime (CPU, CoreML on macOS, XNNPACK) with the plugin-EP ABI (RegisterExecutionProviderLibrary / GetEpDevices / AppendExecutionProvider_V2): the host of the TensorRT-RTX, OpenVINO and QNN plugin EPs. 1.30 is the newest version inside the TensorRT-RTX EP 0.5 test matrix (ORT 1.25.0-1.30.0). MIT.
core.macosNote: macOS arm64 comes from the same NuGet package (runtimes/osx-arm64/native/libonnxruntime.dylib, CoreML EP inside; seen in CI run 45623071458's package listing). ONNX Runtime's GitHub release has no osx archive for 1.30.0. Intel Macs (osx-x64): ONNX Runtime stopped publishing x86_64 macOS builds after 1.23. nuget.org's catalog entries list runtimes/osx-x64/native/libonnxruntime.dylib for 1.22.0 and 1.23.2, but for 1.24.1, 1.24.4 and every later version up to 1.32.0 only osx-arm64; pypi.org's onnxruntime wheels for macOS x86_64 also stop at 1.23.2. So osx-x64 takes 1.23.2, the newest x86_64 build (C API 23: pmml asks for the newest API both sides know, from its header version down to 14, and calls the plugin-EP functions only from API 22/23 on; CoreML through the generic SessionOptionsAppendExecutionProvider). Its pin is the SHA-512 nuget.org publishes for the package (catalog entry packageHash sVAnmG5x...Fgs2mA==, packageHashAlgorithm SHA512, packageSize 123371574, read from the catalog API without downloading; the entry lists runtimes/osx-x64/native/libonnxruntime.dylib, 39742608 bytes). Builds keep the core version's C API headers (headersFrom nupkg).

directml.what: ONNX Runtime with the DirectML EP (any D3D12 GPU; zero-copy with D3D12 resources). 1.24.4 is the last DirectML build Microsoft published (DirectML is 'legacy' in Windows ML); it still has the plugin-EP ABI v24. MIT.

directmlRuntime.what: DirectML redistributable (the DirectML.dll the directml flavor loads; same pin as PushFPS 4.5.3's prepare_runtime.py)

migraphx.what: ONNX Runtime with the MIGraphX EP (AMD ROCm on Linux, RDNA3/4 and Instinct). The wheel is used as an archive: onnxruntime/capi/*.so. Needs ROCm/MIGraphX installed by the distribution. MIT.

winmlCatalog.what: Windows ML (Microsoft.Windows.AI.MachineLearning, standalone, unpackaged; reg-free WinRT, no Windows App SDK runtime) for its ExecutionProviderCatalog flat C API (WinMLEpCatalog*), which pmml_winml_ep.exe uses to get the EPs that exist only through the catalog (eps with "version": "catalog": AMD's AMDGPUExecutionProvider, min. 2.5.96). Extracted into <Out>\winml only when such an EP is asked for; ONNX Runtime from this package is NOT used by pmml (ort/core is). MIT.
winmlCatalog.note: Pinned by SHA-512, the hash nuget.org publishes for the package (catalog entry packageHash, base64 CQPvpwxc...yCcmQ==, packageHashAlgorithm SHA512, packageSize 52171134; read from the catalog API without downloading the package). The catalog entry lists runtimes/win-x64, win-arm64 and win-arm64ec native/{Microsoft.Windows.AI.MachineLearning,onnxruntime,DirectML}.dll.

trt-rtx.what: NVIDIA TensorRT for RTX as an ONNX Runtime plugin EP (NVIDIA/TensorRT-RTX-EP-ABI 0.5.0; bundles the TensorRT-RTX 1.7 runtime). RTX GPUs; JIT engine build on the user's GPU, cached. Host: ort/core.

openvino.what: Intel OpenVINO as an ONNX Runtime plugin EP (Intel.ML.OnnxRuntime.EP.OpenVINO 1.8.1): Arc / Xe iGPU (XMX), Intel NPU, CPU. Host: ort/core. Apache-2.0.
openvino.note: On Windows every OpenVINO DLL carries an embedded manifest that depends on the private side-by-side assembly 'openvino_runtime' 1.8.1.0, described by openvino_runtime.manifest next to them: without that file each LoadLibrary fails with error 14001 (sxstrace: 'Resolving reference openvino_runtime ... Activation Context generation failed', CI run 45643575147). The .manifest files are extracted with the DLLs.

webgpu.what: ONNX Runtime's WebGPU EP as a plugin EP (onnxruntime-ep-webgpu 0.5.0; Dawn on Vulkan on Linux): any Vulkan GPU, the second ONNX Runtime candidate next to ncnn where no vendor EP runs (AMD without ROCm, Intel next to OpenVINO, other Vulkan GPUs). Needs ORT >= 1.24.4 and the system's libvulkan.so.1. Host: ort/core. MIT.
webgpu.note: The wheel holds one library, onnxruntime_ep_webgpu/libonnxruntime_providers_webgpu.so (its zip directory, 0.5.0). 0.5.0 (2026-10-29) rather than 0.6.0 (2026-11-16): the newer one was under two weeks old at pin time.

qnn.what: Qualcomm QNN (Hexagon NPU, Adreno GPU backend) as an ONNX Runtime plugin EP (onnxruntime-qnn 2.8.0, needs ORT >= 1.24.2). Snapdragon X on Windows ARM64. Host: ort/core.
qnn.note: The win_amd64 wheel carries both amd64 and arm64ec libraries under libs/<arch>/: only the platform's own folder is extracted (a flat extract let arm64ec overwrite amd64, CI run 45603367125). The win-arm64 layout is unverified (no ARM64 Windows run yet).

amdgpu.what: AMD's AMDGPUExecutionProvider exists only through the Windows ML ExecutionProviderCatalog (Windows 11 24H2+, Adrenalin 24.12.1+); PyPI has a 0.0.0 placeholder only. pmml registers whatever EP library the catalog reports (PMML_EP_LIBRARY / eps/amdgpu/ep.json written by the installer); until then AMD on Windows runs DirectML.

ncnn.what: Tencent ncnn with Vulkan (BSD-3), prebuilt release packages; linked statically into pmml's ncnn backend (Linux/macOS/Windows any Vulkan GPU, MoltenVK on macOS).

osx.what: the Vulkan build (macos.zip is CPU-only); Vulkan through MoltenVK (Homebrew molten-vk)

source.what: the full source with submodules (glslang), for builds no prebuilt package fits: manylinux_2_28 (glibc 2.28), static and PIC, simplevk (dlopens libvulkan.so.1 at run time) and simpleomp

models.what: RIFE v4.25 lite and v4.26 (the releases PushFlow's tiers use) as ncnn models with the rife.Warp layer, from VapourSynth-RIFE-ncnn-Vulkan (MIT, Copyright HolyWu; weights by hzwer, MIT) at a pinned commit. Used by pmml's ncnn backend. PushFlow's own ONNX exports do not convert with pnnx (it refuses their batch-of-two warps: 'split along batch axis 0 is not supported', CI run 45608301357); nihui's rife-ncnn-vulkan model set stops at v4.6.

pushflow.what: PushFlow's RIFE models exactly as PushFPS ships them: scripts/pushflow/prepare_runtime.py at the PushFPS tag in scripts/pushfps-pin.json (vs-mlrt external-models rife_v4.25_lite / rife_v4.26, MIT weights by hzwer, with the grid and mask outputs added). An installed PushFPS (runtime/experimental/pushflow) is used as is when its models.json hashes match.

synth.what: pmml's own small graphs (pmml/scripts/make_graphs.py, GPL-3.0): pack (full-size frames -> the network's padded input), synth (rebuild at full size from the network's grids and mask, and 'flow once, synthesize many' for further timesteps). Generated at build time; deterministic.

clips.what: Public test clips for the correctness and quality checks (CI only): Xiph derf 720p50 Y4M (the first 24 frames by an HTTP range; one frame is 1382406 bytes)
